paragraphs.english: That everyone’s too busy these days is a cliché. But one specific complaint is made especially mournfully: There’s never any time to read.
paragraphs.chinese: 如今人人都太忙了，这已经是老生常谈。不过，有一种抱怨尤其带着哀叹：总是没有时间读书。

paragraphs.english: What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don’t seem sufficient. The web’s full of articles offering tips on making time to read: “Give up TV” or “Carry a book with you at all times.” But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn’t work. Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning — or else you’re so exhausted that a challenging book’s the last thing you need. The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, “is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication... It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption.” Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can’t be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
paragraphs.chinese: 让问题更加棘手的是，通常的时间管理技巧似乎并不足以解决它。网上到处都是教人腾出阅读时间的文章，比如“放弃看电视”或“随时随身带一本书”。但以我的经验，用这些方法偶尔省出三十分钟并不管用。坐下来读书时，与工作有关的思绪仍像飞轮一样转个不停；要不就是你已经累得不行，最不想面对的正是一本需要费力阅读的书。小说家兼评论家蒂姆·帕克斯写道，现代人的头脑“极度倾向于交流……问题不只是人会受到打扰，而是人实际上就有被打扰的倾向”。深度阅读需要的不只是时间，还需要一种特殊的时间，而单纯提高效率并不能获得它。

paragraphs.english: In fact, “becoming more efficient” is part of the problem. Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal. Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting. Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you’ll manage only goal-focused reading — useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind. “The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt,” writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and “we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them.” No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.
paragraphs.chinese: 事实上，“变得更高效”本身就是问题的一部分。把时间视为应当尽可能充分利用的资源，就意味着你会以工具性的方式对待它，只有某一刻能推动你向某个目标前进时，才觉得这段时间花得值得。相比之下，沉浸式阅读需要你愿意冒着低效、没有目标，甚至浪费时间的风险。如果试图把它当作待办事项硬塞进时间表，你最多只能做到以目标为导向的阅读——这种阅读有时很有用，却并非最令人满足的那一种。加里·埃伯利在《神圣的时间》中写道：“未来如同空瓶子，沿着一条无法停止、近乎无限的传送带向我们而来。”而且，“当这些大小不同的瓶子——天、小时、分钟——经过时，我们感到必须把它们装满，因为如果它们空着过去了，我们就浪费了它们。”若想沉浸于一本书，再没有比这种心态更糟糕的了。

paragraphs.english: So what does work? Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading. You’d think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us “step outside time’s flow” into “soul time.” You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers. “Carry a book with you at all times” can actually work, too — providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down. On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you’re “making time to read,” but just reading, and making time for everything else.
paragraphs.chinese: 那么什么办法才有效？答案或许出人意料：固定安排阅读时间。你可能觉得，这会助长追求效率的心态，但埃伯利指出，实际上这种仪式性的行为有助于我们“走出时间之流”，进入“灵魂的时间”。你可以只读纸质书，或使用功能单一的电子阅读器，以减少干扰。“随时随身带一本书”其实也能奏效，前提是你足够频繁地翻阅它，让阅读成为一种默认状态：你只是偶尔从中浮上来处理事务，随后再沉下去。状态特别好的时候，你不再觉得自己是在“腾出时间阅读”，而只是一直在读书，抽时间做其他所有事情。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: Thinking of time as a resource means you approach it instrumentally.
sentenceNotes.structure: 动名词短语 Thinking ... 作主语；to be maximised 后置修饰 resource；means 后省略 that 引导宾语从句；judging ... 为伴随状语；in so far as 引导限定判断成立范围的从句。
sentenceNotes.translation: 把时间视为应尽可能充分利用的资源，意味着你以工具性方式对待时间，只有某一刻有助于接近目标时，才认为它花得值得。
sentenceNotes.tip: 句子的主语是整个 Thinking 短语；only 限制“何时才算时间花得值”。

sentenceNotes.sentence: “Carry a book with you at all times” can actually work, too — providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: “Carry a book with you at all times” can actually work, too.
sentenceNotes.structure: providing 引导条件状语从句；so that 引导结果从句；from which 引导定语从句，修饰 default state；before dropping ... 表示处理事务后再回到阅读。
sentenceNotes.translation: “随时随身带一本书”也确实有效，前提是你经常翻阅，让阅读成为默认状态，你只是暂时从中浮出来办事，随后再回去。
sentenceNotes.tip: dip in、surface、dropping back down 构成同一组潜入与浮出的比喻。
